why: The student uses the documented wrong rule that a local variable gets a default value of 0 when it is declared. In Java, reading an unassigned local c is a compile error ('variable c might not have been initialized'), so the answer is wrong and prestructural.

concepts.quote: int c; declares c, so c is 0.
concepts.why: A declaration without an initializer leaves a local variable unassigned. It does not set it to 0.
The answer makes no claim about int arithmetic or int's range.
A local variable must be assigned before it is read, so println(c + 1) does not compile.
The answer says nothing about double.
